title: A television under warranty
body: Mrs Krishna bought a colour television from a local dealer for Rs 30,000 and was given a six-month warranty card and a bill. The set stopped working after three months. When she complained to the dealer, an engineer was sent to repair it, but the television continued to give trouble. She complained again, both to the dealer and to the company's branch office, but no one replied. Her neighbour told her that nothing could be done because the dealer had already tried once to repair the set. Another friend suggested that she should go straight to the highest consumer authority in New Delhi. Mrs Krishna still has the bill and the warranty card and is now thinking about what to do next.
